reports.title: Wisconsin OWI Racial Disparities Analysis
reports.short_finding: Black defendants receive roughly 7 additional jail days and substantially higher 180-day recidivism, signaling harsher penalties. However, race estimates are sensitive to specification and flip sign once prior convictions are controlled, while the legal drinking age (21) is associated with 27 additional jail days—suggesting age markers for behavioral severity operate more powerfully than race in sentencing decisions.

reports.title: Texas SB 3 / ERCOT Analysis
reports.short_finding: SB 3 weatherization mandates increased generator capacity factors by 1.8 percentage points relative to neighboring states, indicating improved cold-weather reliability. This gain accompanied a 1.1 cent/kWh increase in retail prices, with plant-level reliability varying substantially across generators with a high concentration of below average firms, while utility-level pricing shows energy retail companies concentrated around the average price.

reports.title: Texas Medicaid Non-Expansion Analysis
reports.short_finding: Event-study DiD estimates find no statistically or economically significant relative change in insurance coverage or health outcomes for low-income Texans after the April 2023 Medicaid unwinding — suggesting Texas's gap population was not clearly left worse off on these margins relative to expansion-state neighbors in Arkansas, Louisiana, and New Mexico. The one statistically significant result is a 1.8-percentage-point widening of cost barriers to care (p < 0.05): financial access deteriorated even where headline enrollment held. The insurance DiD (+7.4 pp) is actually positive — the gap narrowed, not widened — consistent with the unwinding having less bite than non-expansion alone might predict. Together, the results indicate that, despite Texas's structural coverage-gap disadvantage, the end of continuous enrollment did not measurably widen coverage or health gaps further, though the cost channel is a real and detectable pressure point.

reports.title: ERCOT Retail Electricity Market Analysis
reports.short_finding: Instrumenting retail price with wholesale cost-shifters (statewide and zone-footprint wholesale prices) flips the endogeneity-biased OLS sign and produces a downward-sloping demand curve with implied own-price elasticities near -3: economically meaningful but statistically insignificant, since every confidence interval brackets zero in the 98 REP-year sample. A separate pre/post regression shows TDU-level retail prices rose about 6.7 cents/kWh (roughly +55%) after Winter Storm Uri while cross-REP dispersion was unchanged, consistent with wholesale cost pass-through.

reports.title: Hurricane Beryl / CenterPoint Consumer-Harm Analysis
reports.short_finding: Hurricane Beryl caused outages disproportionately concentrated in lower-income Harris County zip codes, with median restoration times exceeding five days in the most-affected areas — a pattern inconsistent with purely storm-severity-driven damage.

reports.title: DOJConst / Constellation-Calpine Merger Analysis
reports.short_finding: Proposed consolidation among Texas electricity generation owners would push post-merger HHI above DOJ thresholds in multiple capacity segments, with simulated market share shifts suggesting meaningful harm to wholesale price competition.
